profile.headline: Secure API Gateway Developer at Optum
profile.summary:
I have a long range of skills I have picked up over the past 25 years of working in IT. But, there are two big things I've learned during that time: never stop learning and once you have one job in IT, you can adapt to almost any direction you want to pursue.

Never stop learning: Technology is ever changing. The minute you stop learning, you become a relic. Learn that new tech that's on the cutting edge. It might not be prolific now, but a version of it will be I use in the near future and you might be able to use it to your advantage. This goes for your everyday life too. Challenge yourself to keep your mind active and growing. Bettering yourself is never a bad thing; It just takes a little work.

You can adapt to any career direction in IT: Technology has become a universal language. Once you figure out the logic, it just takes a slight shift to either change your position or to learn a new role entirely. You might need a new mindset to slide into some of those roles, but you can do it if you put your mind to it.

IT has many lessons to give. I've learned to roll with the punches, and get back up after failure. I've learned a good team can overcome any obstacles. I've learned to lift up your colleagues, because when they do better, you can do better. I've learned leadership isn't always given to those that deserve it, so cherish those leaders you encounter along the way that know what they're doing.

What life experiences has it given you?

positions.title: Sr. Software Developer
positions.description: Manage and support secure Kong API Gateways deployed in both Privately and Publicly hosted Kubernetes clusters. Use Github and Github Actions for CI/CD to maintain a highly available and up to date environment. Use Splunk and Grafana to help users troubleshoot their own API performance.

positions.title: Private Cloud Developer
positions.description: Develop and support multiple private cloud technologies. Manage and maintain OpenShift, Origin, and Kubernetes clusters.

positions.title: Senior UNIX Analyst
positions.description:
I am the primary Linux SME supporting over 300 servers in locations across the globe as a member of the Server, Storage, and Backup team at Starkey. When I first started working here, all Linux authentication was local and management of hosts was all manual. I have since deployed Red Hat Identity Management, Puppet OpenSource, and Ansible to manage our fleet. I have managed our Satellite infrastructure for our small Linux footprint which has started to grow as the direction of our organization has changed. I have used Python with a smattering of Ruby to integrate all of these tools to try to bring some additional automation into our environment.

*Support 300+ virtualized and physical servers running RedHat.
*Managed Red Hat Satellite for the Linux fleet
*Managed servers on Cisco UCS, Dell, and HP
*Utilized Puppet for centralized configuration management

Skill & Knowledge:
RedHat Enterprise Linux 4, 5, 6, 7
Puppet
Ansible Base and Tower
Red Hat Identity Management
VMWare
SumoLogic
Python and shell scripting

positions.title: Server Operations-Lead Engineer
positions.description:
Team lead for the UNIX Operations which supports over 1000 servers in locations across the globe.

 *Support 1000+ virtualized and physical servers running both RedHat and Solaris.
 *Directly involved with setting up Spacewalk to patch our Linux fleet.
 *Directly involved with the team integrating RedHat OpenShift Enterprise for use in FICO's offerings.
 *Managed servers on Cisco UCS, HP, and SPARC platforms
 *Integrated root password management with CyberArk
 *Configured core utilities (DNS, DHCP, Spacewalk) in FICO's cloud environments
 *Utilized Puppet for centralized configuration management

Skill & Knowledge:
 Solaris 9 & 10
 RedHat Enterprise Linux 4, 5, 6
 RedHat OpenShift Enterprise
 Spacewalk
 Puppet
 CyberArk
 VMWare
 Veritas Storage Foundation and Cluster
 ZFS
 LVM

positions.description: Maintained Solaris, AIX, and HP-UX servers. Managed VCS clusters. Built  Solaris and Redhat servers.

positions.description: Monitored and maintained primarily servers running the Solaris OS.  I was on the on-call rotation which required me to support AIX, HP-UX, and RedHat Linux as well as Solaris.
